notes: PILOT: overfitting controls and seed ensembling. Stack on the base: python -m dskit.pipeline workflow configs/workflow.json --args configs/pilot-base.json --args configs/pilot-regularize.json. Earlier neural runs fit training rows well and validation badly (QQQ about +9% train skill against -22% development), the signature of variance, not bias. The step-6 grid here fixes width and learning rate at the manifest defaults and crosses weight decay (0.01 = the TorchCDF default, 1.0: AdamW decay is decoupled, shrinking weights by about learning_rate x weight_decay per step, so at lr 0.001 and a few hundred early-stopped steps 0.1 is barely distinguishable from 0.01 in a synthetic smoke run; 1.0 is a real contrast), dropout (0, 0.2) and seeds (one, or five fits averaged into one mixture): 8 candidates. The warm-up search table (step6 rounds and selection/candidates.jsonl) shows each control's effect; the selected one is then evaluated on the scored folds as usual. Five-seed candidates cost five times as much to train.
